fig1_roots.svg: The five 5th-roots of $1$ (blue, from roots_of_unity) lie on the unit circle, spaced $72^\circ$ apart and summing to $0$. The five 5th-roots of $32i$ (orange, from nth_roots) sit on a circle of radius $32^{1/5}=2$, rotated by $\arg(32i)/5$: every nonzero $z$ has exactly $n$ roots, evenly spaced by $2\pi/n$ at radius $r^{1/n}$.
fig2_branch_cut.svg: The imaginary part of the principal logarithm, $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Log}\,z=\arg z$, over the complex plane (computed from principal_log). It is single-valued in $(-\pi,\pi]$ but jumps by $2\pi$ across the negative real axis — the branch cut (dashed). Crossing it flips $\sqrt z$ in sign and shifts $\mathrm{Log}\,z$ by $2\pi i$.
